title: Selectivity and Escape at One Pocket

scenes.visual: Schematic grid of twelve slate-blue (#4A90D9) two-lobed kinase blocks fills the frame; glowing amber-gold (#E8A838) ATP tokens drift gently toward their clefts. Crisp white title fades in at top: 'Selectivity and Escape at One Pocket' (labelled 'schematic').

scenes.tts: About five hundred human kinases hold A T P in nearly the same pocket. How can one small drug shut down just one kinase? And what can you do when a tumour fights back?
scenes.caption: About five hundred human kinases hold ATP in nearly the same pocket. How can one small drug shut down just one kinase? And what can you do when a tumour fights back?
scenes.visual: The schematic grid of slate-blue kinase blocks expands to suggest ~500 conserved pockets, with label 'About 500 human kinases' (size 30). Amber-gold ATP tokens dock smoothly into every cleft while one bright teal (#2EC4B6) drug block hovers above the grid.
scenes.narration: About five hundred human kinases hold ATP in nearly the same pocket. How can one small drug shut down just one kinase? And what can you do when a tumour fights back?

scenes.tts: Every protein kinase moves the end phosphate of A T P onto another protein. To run that transfer, active kinases fold their pockets into nearly the same shape. That is why one pocket's drug was expected to jam dozens.
scenes.caption: Every protein kinase moves the end phosphate of ATP onto another protein. To run that transfer, active kinases fold their pockets into nearly the same shape. That is why one pocket's drug was expected to jam dozens.
scenes.visual: Camera zooms smoothly onto three slate-blue active kinases side by side. In each cleft, an amber-gold ATP hands a small glowing phosphate bead onto a target block; all three active clefts highlight with identical outlines as the teal drug appears to fit all three.
scenes.narration: Every protein kinase moves the end phosphate of ATP onto another protein. To run that transfer, active kinases fold their pockets into nearly the same shape. That is why one pocket's drug was expected to jam dozens.

scenes.tts: Imatinib broke that rule in two ways. First, working shapes must match, yet switched-off shapes are thought to differ between kinases. Imatinib fits an idle shape that few kinases adopt the same way. So it hits a short list: A B L, the P D G F receptor, and Kit.
scenes.caption: Imatinib broke that rule in two ways. First, working shapes must match, yet switched-off shapes are thought to differ between kinases. Imatinib fits an idle shape that few kinases adopt the same way. So it hits a short list: ABL, the PDGF receptor, and KIT.
scenes.visual: The three slate-blue kinases relax into distinct switched-off shapes (labelled 'Idle shapes thought to differ — schematic'). The bright teal imatinib block slides snugly into the idle ABL cleft, while bouncing cleanly off two unrelated kinase shapes; a concise side tally shows 'Short list: ABL, PDGFR, KIT'.
scenes.narration: Imatinib broke that rule in two ways. First, working shapes must match, yet switched-off shapes are thought to differ between kinases. Imatinib fits an idle shape that few kinases adopt the same way. So it hits a short list: ABL, the PDGF receptor, and KIT.

scenes.tts: Still, normal cells use those same three kinases. So the second layer is target dependence: how much a cell relies on the blocked kinase. Chronic myeloid leukaemia cells carry a fused, always-on kinase, B C R A B L, and cannot live without it. Normal cells tolerate a pause, though tissue injury can still occur.
scenes.caption: Still, normal cells use those same three kinases. So the second layer is target dependence: how much a cell relies on the blocked kinase. Chronic myeloid leukaemia cells carry a fused, always-on kinase, BCR-ABL, and cannot live without it. Normal cells tolerate a pause, though tissue injury can still occur.
scenes.visual: The frame splits into two schematic cells: left, a dividing leukaemia cell driven by a glowing emerald-green (#4CAF50) arrow from fused slate-blue BCR-ABL; right, a normal cell with ABL, PDGFR, and KIT. Bright teal imatinib enters both cells; the leukaemia growth arrow fades to grey and the cell shrinks, while the normal cell slows slightly and stays intact (caption tag: 'Tissue injury still possible').
scenes.narration: Still, normal cells use those same three kinases. So the second layer is target dependence: how much a cell relies on the blocked kinase. Chronic myeloid leukaemia cells carry a fused, always-on kinase, BCR-ABL, and cannot live without it. Normal cells tolerate a pause, though tissue injury can still occur.

scenes.tts: Then came a sharp turn. Some patients who improved on imatinib later relapsed. Sequencing B C R A B L from their blood revealed a single changed residue at position three fifteen. Threonine had turned into isoleucine, a bulkier side chain sitting beside the drug.
scenes.caption: Then came a sharp turn. Some patients who improved on imatinib later relapsed. Sequencing BCR-ABL from their blood revealed a single changed residue at position 315. Threonine had turned into isoleucine, a bulkier side chain sitting beside the drug.
scenes.visual: Zoom back into the slate-blue ABL pocket inside a rebounding leukaemia cell. A small neat nub on the pocket wall labelled 'Thr 315' morphs into a large, protruding coral-red (#E05A47) block labelled 'Ile 315' as a subtle gene strip flips 'ACT -> ATT' above.
scenes.narration: Then came a sharp turn. Some patients who improved on imatinib later relapsed. Sequencing BCR-ABL from their blood revealed a single changed residue at position 315. Threonine had turned into isoleucine, a bulkier side chain sitting beside the drug.

scenes.tts: Position three fifteen is called the gatekeeper residue, because it guards a back alcove beside the A T P site. Imatinib reaches inside and makes a hydrogen bond with threonine. Bulkier isoleucine cannot make that bond, and it blocks imatinib. Yet A T P never uses the alcove, so the kinase keeps firing.
scenes.caption: Position 315 is called the gatekeeper residue, because it guards a back alcove beside the ATP site. Imatinib reaches inside and makes a hydrogen bond with threonine. Bulkier isoleucine cannot make that bond, and it blocks imatinib. Yet ATP never uses the alcove, so the kinase keeps firing.
scenes.visual: Cross-section schematic of the slate-blue cleft highlights the deeper alcove labelled 'Back alcove' guarded by 'Gatekeeper 315'. With Thr 315, teal imatinib forms a dotted hydrogen bond and locks the pocket. Flipping to coral-red Ile 315 snaps the dotted hydrogen bond and bumps imatinib out, while amber-gold ATP enters smoothly and lights up the emerald-green signal arrow.
scenes.narration: Position 315 is called the gatekeeper residue, because it guards a back alcove beside the ATP site. Imatinib reaches inside and makes a hydrogen bond with threonine. Bulkier isoleucine cannot make that bond, and it blocks imatinib. Yet ATP never uses the alcove, so the kinase keeps firing.

scenes.tts: A relapse feels like failure, yet it works like an experiment. Changing one drug contact, with catalysis intact, is strong evidence that imatinib hit the right target. The tumour still needed that kinase. Pause and predict. To beat this mutant, how must the next drug change at position three fifteen?
scenes.caption: A relapse feels like failure, yet it works like an experiment. Changing one drug contact, with catalysis intact, is strong evidence that imatinib hit the right target. The tumour still needed that kinase. Pause and predict. To beat this mutant, how must the next drug change at position 315?
scenes.visual: The emerald-green signal arrow pulses while teal imatinib repeatedly bounces off coral-red Ile 315. A clean banner rises above the pocket: 'Predict: How must the next drug change at position 315?'
scenes.narration: A relapse feels like failure, yet it works like an experiment. Changing one drug contact, with catalysis intact, is strong evidence that imatinib hit the right target. The tumour still needed that kinase. Pause and predict. To beat this mutant, how must the next drug change at position 315?

scenes.visual: The predict banner stays crisp and legible on screen while coral-red Ile 315 pulses slowly in the slate-blue pocket and a subtle circular 4.5-second progress ring sweeps around the corner.

scenes.tts: Because imatinib's hold depends on threonine three fifteen, the next drug had to grip without that contact. So chemists gave ponatinib a slim, straight carbon-carbon triple bond right where isoleucine sticks out. That slender bridge clears the bulky side chain, so ponatinib shuts down the mutant kinase.
scenes.caption: Because imatinib's hold depends on threonine 315, the next drug had to grip without that contact. So chemists gave ponatinib a slim, straight carbon-carbon triple bond right where isoleucine sticks out. That slender bridge clears the bulky side chain, so ponatinib shuts down the mutant kinase.
scenes.visual: The bulky teal imatinib block transforms smoothly into a new teal ponatinib block with a thin, straight central bar labelled 'Slim triple-bond bridge'. It glides cleanly past coral-red Ile 315 into the slate-blue pocket; amber-gold ATP is blocked and the emerald-green signal arrow fades to muted grey.
scenes.narration: Because imatinib's hold depends on threonine 315, the next drug had to grip without that contact. So chemists gave ponatinib a slim, straight carbon-carbon triple bond right where isoleucine sticks out. That slender bridge clears the bulky side chain, so ponatinib shuts down the mutant kinase.

scenes.tts: Hold two principles as you read on. Where a drug binds shapes its selectivity, alongside how much the tumour relies on that target. And when resistance alters a drug contact, reading that escape guides the next drug.
scenes.caption: Hold two principles as you read on. Where a drug binds shapes its selectivity, alongside how much the tumour relies on that target. And when resistance alters a drug contact, reading that escape guides the next drug.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back cleanly to show two paired schematic panels: left, teal imatinib docked in the idle slate-blue pocket ('Shape + target dependence'); right, coral-red Ile 315 with teal ponatinib sliding past ('Escape -> next drug'). Both fade smoothly into a dark slate backdrop.
scenes.narration: Hold two principles as you read on. Where a drug binds shapes its selectivity, alongside how much the tumour relies on that target. And when resistance alters a drug contact, reading that escape guides the next drug.

scenes.visual: Clean full-frame end card on dark slate background showing one crisp white sentence only: 'Where a drug binds shapes selectivity, and escape guides the next drug.'
